reasoning: Commercial and industrial (C&I) loans are a weekly series that tends to show gradual trends rather than sharp week-to-week changes. Looking at historical patterns, C&I loans have shown modest growth in recent years, though they can fluctuate based on economic conditions and business demand. Week-to-week changes are relatively small and can go either direction. Given the short one-week timeframe and typical volatility, this is close to a coin flip with slight bias toward increase given general economic growth trends. Historical data suggests increases occur roughly 50-55% of weeks.
